newsitem.title: USA: McDonald's new ads focus on new Deluxe sandwiches.
newsitem.headline: McDonald's new ads focus on new Deluxe sandwiches.

text.p: McDonald's Corp will be selling more of the steak -- or, rather, chicken and fish -- than the sizzle in new advertising launching its new Deluxe Grilled Chicken, Fish Filet and Crispy Chicken sandwiches.

Continuing the "Sandwiches with a grown-up taste" theme, the new advertising features more product and more adults. Gone are the shots of kids turning up their noses to adult sandwiches, images that dominated the estimated $100 million launch of the Arch Deluxe hamburger four months ago.

The new advertising, also created by Fallon McElligott, Minneapolis, plays to adults and adult humor. "We had fun with it," said David Green, McDonald's senior vice president of marketing. "You can't take yourself too seriously."

McDonald's use of Fallon McElligott for the Arch Deluxe burger introduction four months ago and for the three new Deluxe sandwiches has fostered speculation about McDonald's' happiness with Leo Burnett USA's role as lead agency.
However, Green said the whole issue has drawn "too much intrigue."
"Having multiple resources is not a new precedent in any shape or form. Our agencies work well together. Leo Burnett is the lead agency and they have fulfilled our expectations," Green said.
In addition to three spots from Fallon McElligott, Burnett contributed a spot.
McDonald's ethnic advertising was handled by Burrell Advertising, Chicago and del Rivero Messianu, Miami.
McDonald's also will continue to run a spot featuring Andrew Selvaggio, the restaurant chain's executive chef, created by DDB Needham Chicago, another McDonald's agency.
